title: The two environment kinds reach the shared runtime contract and the generated client
description:
Prerequisite LEAF carved out of task-a2409cba9ad841a690961692a2948c41 by worker-caece97b (acting as architect on a claimed PLANNING row), 2026-09-05. Second of two leaves; the other is task-d0d1cb5c3f034d50bd84b7ed56b7e812 (the MCP/human-only fence). a2409cba measured 13 forced file edits against the 10-file cap and submit_plan refused it at 11 with [CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION]. Parent chain: SPIDR child 1b of task-9ae492b373fa4e7aa6b1e91585f6e612.

WHY THIS SEAM IS REAL, unlike the one tried first. The daemon's PAYLOAD_KEYS roster and the shared RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS roster are deliberately NOT set-equal, and the codebase says so in its own words at apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-create-with-source.ts:35 - "kind `goal.create_with_source` is in `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` but NOT in" the daemon table. A kind may therefore exist on the shared contract with no daemon registry entry: an established, deliberate state, not a hole this row invents.

CONTRAST, so nobody re-proposes the OTHER split: apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238 DOES weld the daemon's PAYLOAD_KEYS to the v2 registry by set-equality, which is why the daemon vocabulary and the daemon registry cannot be separated and stay together in a2409cba.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS in packages/contracts, its hand-transcribed test roster, and the REGENERATED control-room client. NO daemon vocabulary, NO PAYLOAD_KEYS, NO registry, NO handler, NO MCP roster - a2409cba and task-d0d1cb5c own those.

MEASURED SEAMS (worker-caece97b at HEAD f3b94eaa):
- packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts:85-117 - RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, a frozen alphabetical tuple. runtime-contract.test.ts:124 asserts sortedness, so insert in sorted position.
- packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-contract.test.ts:103-104 - `expect(RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS).toEqual(EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS)` against a HAND-TRANSCRIBED list, plus a LITERAL count of 102. That file's own header at :30-32 explains a derived expectation would be vacuous. Transcribe by hand; do NOT replace it with RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS.length.
- packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.js is `export * from "./runtime-vocabulary.ts";` - a star re-export. NO EDIT NEEDED.
- packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:907 - GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST, currently ed5f6b87cfca761b4389d66429046f5f2420f9fa04a373c1f22ab0608bfb8076. Re-read it rather than trusting this value.
- packages/control-room-client/package.json:18 - the generator is `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`.
- TWO GREEN-CHECKS, NOT EDITS: src/contract-digest.test.ts:21 (deriveContractDigest equals the pin) and src/generated-coverage.test.ts:89-90 (generated builder set equals RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, asserted in BOTH directions). Both go green on their own once the generator runs. If either needs hand-editing, the generator did not run or the contract edit was wrong.
- apps/daemon/src/cutover/v2-surface-manifest.ts:86 builds GLOBAL_COMMANDS from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS. Check it does not demand a matching daemon entry before assuming the daemon suite stays green.
definitionOfDone: `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` are members of RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS in packages/contracts, inserted in SORTED position (runtime-contract.test.ts:124 asserts sortedness).

runtime-contract.test.ts gains both kinds in its HAND-TRANSCRIBED EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS and its literal count moves 102 -> 104, with the transcribed form preserved - replacing it with a derived length is a regression that file's header at :30-32 forbids. Prove the arm still bites: remove ONE kind from the production roster, confirm the test REDS, restore.

The generated client is REGENERATED with `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`, never hand-edited, and BOTH the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST are quoted verbatim in the completion record.

contract-digest.test.ts and generated-coverage.test.ts are GREEN WITHOUT BEING EDITED - quote their `Test Files N passed` count line. If either required an edit, say so and explain why, because it means the generator was bypassed.

Name `goal.create_with_source` as the precedent that makes this intermediate state legitimate.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm test` (the root include DOES cover packages/**, so this row is genuinely covered by it), `pnpm typecheck`, and the daemon run above as the attribution baseline.

ADD ONLY, IN SORTED POSITION. Do not reorder or remove any existing kind - runtime-contract.test.ts asserts both the exact roster and its sortedness, and a reorder is the silent edit those arms exist to catch.

NO DAEMON WORK. Do not touch daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, PAYLOAD_KEYS, the registry, the MCP roster or HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS - those belong to task-a2409cba and task-d0d1cb5c. Adding these kinds to the daemon's PAYLOAD_KEYS here would red daemon-store-dependencies.test.ts:238.

A kind on the shared contract with no daemon registry entry is a DELIBERATE, EXISTING state - goal.create_with_source is the precedent (goal-create-with-source.ts:35). Do not 'complete' the wiring to make it look finished.

implementationPlan.description: BASELINE AND PREMISE RE-MEASURE, before any edit. (a) Record HEAD sha and `git status --porcelain` for the six owned paths, so foreign dirt is distinguishable from mine later. (b) Capture the MERGE-BASE gate state for global rail 3 attribution: run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm test` NOW, and save the failing-file lists verbatim. These are the (1) term of the (2)-minus-(1) delta; without them a pre-existing foreign red cannot be told from one I caused. (c) Re-census the digest mirrors with `git grep -n ed5f6b87cfca761b4389d66429046f5f2420f9fa04a373c1f22ab0608bfb8076 -- ':!.moe' ':!*.jsonl'` and confirm the four sites are still exactly generated-client.ts:907, generated-coverage.test.ts:36, data-adapter.test.ts:18, approve-plan.test.tsx:255. (d) Confirm `environment.set_variable` and `environment.unset_variable` are still ABSENT from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS, and that the live count is 104 (the description says 102 and is stale - the comment on runtime-contract.test.ts:104 says 102 while the assertion on :105 says 104). If any premise has moved, stop and re-plan rather than editing against a stale measurement.

ADD THE TWO KINDS TO THE PRODUCTION ROSTER, IN SORTED POSITION, ADD-ONLY. In `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` insert `"environment.set_variable", "environment.unset_variable"` between `"effect.reconcile"` and `"escalation.decide"` - verified by codepoint ordering ('effect' < 'environment' < 'escalation'; 's' < 'u'). Reorder nothing, remove nothing, reflow no unrelated line: runtime-contract.test.ts asserts BOTH the exact roster AND its sortedness against the production tuple, and a silent reorder is precisely what those two arms exist to catch. Do not touch RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS or RUNTIME_TELEMETRY_KINDS.

MIRROR THE ADDITION INTO THE HAND-TRANSCRIBED TEST ROSTER AND MOVE THE LITERAL COUNT 104 -> 106. In `EXPECTED_COMMAND_KINDS`, hand-transcribe the same two members at the same sorted position - do NOT paste from the production tuple mechanically and do NOT replace the roster with a derived expression: the file's own header at :29-33 says an expectation computed from the tuple under test can never fail. Change `expect(commands.size).toBe(104)` to `toBe(106)`, and FIX the adjacent stale comment which still reads 'Literal 102' while the assertion said 104 - it must name the number actually asserted. Leave the sortedness arm, the frozen-tuple arm and the query/telemetry arms untouched. Then run `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test` and quote its `Test Files N passed` count line.

PROVE THE ROSTER ARM STILL BITES (DoD 2's mutation drill). Both targets are TRACKED files, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof. D1: delete ONE kind from the PRODUCTION tuple in runtime-vocabulary.ts, run `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`, confirm it REDS naming the roster/count arm, restore, then in a SEPARATE command prove `git diff -- packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts` is empty apart from the step-2 addition. D2: move `environment.set_variable` OUT of sorted position (e.g. to the end of the tuple) and confirm the sortedness arm at :124 reds with the mismatch object - this proves the second arm independently, because a mistranscription that copies the wrong order into the hand roster would leave D1 green. Restore and prove restore separately. Re-run the contracts leg green afterwards and quote the count line. Record both red messages verbatim in the step note; a drill whose red is not quoted proves nothing.

REGENERATE THE CLIENT - never hand-edit it (task rail 1). Read and record the OLD `GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST` from packages/control-room-client/src/generated/generated-client.ts:907 verbatim (expected ed5f6b87cfca761b4389d66429046f5f2420f9fa04a373c1f22ab0608bfb8076, but re-read rather than trust it). Run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate`. Read the NEW digest verbatim. Confirm by `git diff --stat` that the generator touched ONLY generated-client.ts, and confirm the diff adds exactly two command builders (`environment.set_variable`, `environment.unset_variable`) and removes none - a diff that removes builders means the generator ran against the wrong contracts copy. Record OLD and NEW digests in the step note; DoD 3 requires both quoted verbatim in the completion record.

ROTATE THE THREE HAND-PINNED DIGEST MIRRORS AND PROVE ZERO STALE REMAIN. The generator writes only the client; these three are hand-kept golden literals and MUST be edited - that is the documented ritual (generated-coverage.test.ts:30-33), NOT generator bypass, and DoD 4's 'without being edited' clause is answered by saying so explicitly. (a) packages/control-room-client/src/generated-coverage.test.ts:35 GENERATED_FILE_SHA256 - recompute as the sha256 of the regenerated file's bytes; :36 CONTRACT_DIGEST - the new digest. (b) apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts:18 contractSchemaHash. (c) apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/approve-plan.test.tsx:255 contractSchemaHash. Do NOT make any of them derive from GENERATED_CONTRACT_PINS - that would have the mirror verify itself against the artifact it exists to pin, the vacuous-assertion defect global rail 1 names. Then re-run the census `git grep -n <OLD digest> -- ':!.moe' ':!*.jsonl'` and require ZERO hits outside .serena/ records, and `git grep -c <NEW digest>` and require exactly the four sites.

RUN THE FULL GATE SET AND ATTRIBUTE EVERY RED. Foreground, one at a time, reading the `Test Files N passed` COUNT LINE not the exit code (a bad --filter name prints 'No projects matched the filters' and exits 0). (1) `pnpm --filter @moe/contracts test`. (2) `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client test` - contract-digest.test.ts:21 and generated-coverage.test.ts:89-90 must be green; if either still reds, the generator was bypassed or the contract edit was wrong. (3) `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` - the leg epic rail 1 mandates; the two apps mirrors are invisible to every other gate. (4) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` - DoD 5's undisturbed-daemon proof; both kinds stay ABSENT from PAYLOAD_KEYS on purpose, with `goal.create_with_source` (goal-create-with-source.ts:35) as the standing precedent that a contract kind with no daemon registry entry is legitimate. Confirm mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts still pins {excluded:11, queries:6, vocabulary:47, wired:42} - unchanged, because that roster derives from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and PAYLOAD_KEYS, not from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS. (5) `pnpm typecheck`. (6) root `pnpm test` for DoD 6. Apply global rail 3 to (4) and (6): HEAD failures minus the step-1 merge-base failures, intersected with my six owned paths, must be EMPTY; report any foreign red verbatim with its file paths, never hidden and never fabricated green. Disclose that tests/** and tools/** resolve @moe/contracts through the root node_modules junction into /tmp/moe-glance-to-main, so root `pnpm test` cannot witness this change for those two directories.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, THEN HANDOFF. Read the whole diff as an attacker: (a) did anything OTHER than the two insertions change in the production tuple - a reflowed line, a dropped member, a reordered pair? Confirm with `git diff` that the roster hunks are pure additions. (b) Is the hand roster genuinely hand-transcribed and still order-sensitive, or did the edit quietly make it derived? (c) Does the tree contain any leftover drill mutation - `git status --porcelain` the two drilled paths and prove clean. (d) Did I touch a daemon path task rail 3 forbids? Grep the diff for daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, PAYLOAD_KEYS, mcp-tool-allowlist.ts, HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS - all must be absent. (e) Are the two new kinds catalogued in STDIO_TOOL_ENTRIES but NOT advertised by wiredMcpToolKinds()? Confirm, because the whole point of the fence is that the contract can name a kind no agent can reach. Then write the Serena handoff memory (task-b3888068-handoff) recording the new digest, the corrected 104->106 count, the stale-description corrections, and the junction hazard, and update mem:gotcha-contract-digest-mirror-set-moved-two-are-in-apps-control-room with the new baseline digest.

Epic rail 1 is explicit and overrides the narrower prose: any row adding a command kind must re-census all four mirrors and must run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`. This is forced work, not scope creep - the alternative is a knowingly red tree.

WHAT I AM NOT TAKING, per task rail 3: no daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, no PAYLOAD_KEYS, no registry entry, no handler, no HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, no mcp-tool-allowlist.ts. task-a2409cba and task-d0d1cb5c own those. 3. THE MUTATION DRILL TOUCHES A TRACKED FILE ONLY. Both drill targets (runtime-vocabulary.ts, runtime-contract.test.ts) are TRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` is a valid restore proof. Prove restore in a call SEPARATE from the restore itself.

4. A STRANDED DRILL MUTANT was reported in apps/control-room/src/data/data-adapter.test.ts earlier today.
